title: Energy Flow & Trophic Cascades
objectives: Apply the 10% rule to energy flow between trophic levels (APES 1.10, 1.11)
Run a controlled experiment by removing one trophic level
Explain a trophic cascade using model data and a real example

steps.title: Briefing

sequence.instruction: Talk to Dr. Hale by the whiteboard.
npcLines: Welcome! Today's question: what happens to a whole ecosystem if we remove the animals at the top?
The terrarium on the left bench is a model habitat: plants, herbivores, carnivores and apex predators, all at their natural balance.
First run it unchanged as your control. Then we'll take the apex predators out.
how: Follow the yellow arrow and the compass at the top of the screen.
Walk with W A S D or the arrow keys. On an iPad, drag the joystick in the bottom-left corner.
When you are close, a button appears at the bottom of the screen. Press E or tap the button.
Read each line, then press Continue.

intro: Energy enters an ecosystem through plants and moves up the food chain when one organism eats another.
At each step only about 10% of the energy is stored in the next level's bodies. The rest is used for living (moving, breathing, staying warm) and lost as heat.
vocab: Producer
An organism that makes its own food from sunlight, like a plant.
Consumer
An organism that eats others. Herbivores eat plants; carnivores eat animals.
Trophic level
An organism's feeding position in a food chain.
Apex predator
A predator at the top of the food chain with no natural predators.
10% rule
About 10% of the energy at one trophic level passes to the next.

steps.title: Control run

sequence.instruction: Step on the food web station's ring and run 120 days without changing anything (your control).
sequence.hint: Use the default starting numbers. If you changed a slider, press Reset to balance first.

feedback.correct: Control recorded. Notice the populations stay steady: the habitat is in balance.
feedback.incorrect: That run had a level missing. Reset to balance and run again.

how: Walk to the food web station (the left bench) and step onto its glowing ring. The experiment panel opens.
On an iPad or phone the panel slides up from the bottom. Close it with ✕ when you are done.
Leave the sliders at their starting values. If you moved one, press 'Reset to balance'.
Press '▶ Run 120 days' and watch the graph. 'Skip to end' finishes it right away.
Your run is saved in the 'Your runs' table.

question.prompt: The plants in a habitat capture 50,000 kJ of energy. Using the 10% rule, how much energy reaches the apex predators (the fourth trophic level)?
help: Count the transfers: plants → herbivores (1), herbivores → carnivores (2), carnivores → apex predators (3).
Each transfer keeps only 10%, so multiply by 0.1 once for each transfer.
Start with 50,000 kJ and multiply by 0.1 three times.
question.example: If plants capture 20,000 kJ, herbivores get 20,000 × 0.1 = 2,000 kJ, and carnivores get 2,000 × 0.1 = 200 kJ.

sequence.hint: Plants → herbivores → carnivores → apex is three transfers. Multiply by 0.1 three times.

feedback.incorrect: Count the transfers: plants → herbivores → carnivores → apex.

intro: A good experiment compares a change against a control: the same setup with nothing changed.
Your control run shows what the habitat does when every trophic level is present.
vocab: Control
The run where nothing is changed, used for comparison.
Variable
Anything that can change in an experiment.

steps.title: Remove the apex predators

sequence.instruction: Set starting apex predators to 0 (keep everything else the same) and run 120 days.

feedback.correct: Experiment recorded. Compare it with your control in the runs table.
feedback.incorrect: Set apex predators to exactly 0 and keep carnivores and herbivores above 0.

how: Go back to the food web station and press 'Reset to balance'.
Drag the 'Starting apex predators' slider all the way to 0. Don't touch the other sliders.

question.prompt: Compared with your control, what happened to the PLANT population by day 120 when apex predators were removed?
help: Find your two runs in the 'Your runs' table below.
Read 'Day 120 plants' for your control (apex above 0) and for this run (apex 0).
Compare them: is the second number bigger, smaller, or about the same?

feedback.correct: Yes. Even though the plants weren't touched, removing animals two levels up changed them.
feedback.incorrect: Compare day-120 plants in your two runs.

question.prompt: Which real event is the best example of a trophic cascade?

options.label: Wolves returned to Yellowstone, elk browsed less, and willows and aspens grew back
A drought reduced grass growth across a prairie
A wildfire burned part of a forest

feedback.correct: Exactly: a change at the top rippled down to the plants.
feedback.incorrect: A trophic cascade starts with a change in predators and ripples down the food chain.

question.prompt: Explain, step by step, why removing the apex predators changed the plants. Use numbers from your control and experiment runs for at least two trophic levels.
help: Start at the top: what happened to the carnivores when the apex predators were gone? Give the numbers from both runs.
Next: what did that change do to the herbivores? Give the numbers.
Last: how did the change in herbivores affect the plants?
Link your steps with words like 'because', 'so' and 'which caused'.

steps.intro: Now change ONE variable: remove the apex predators. Keep everything else the same as your control so any difference must be caused by that change.
vocab: Independent variable
The one thing YOU change (here: number of apex predators).
Dependent variable
What you measure to see the effect (here: the populations on day 120).
Trophic cascade
When a change at the top of a food chain ripples down through the levels below.

sequence.instruction: Report your findings to Dr. Hale.
npcLines: So the predators at the top were quietly protecting the plants at the bottom. That's a trophic cascade.
This is why ecologists worry about losing top predators to hunting and habitat loss: the effects travel all the way down the food web.
how: Walk to Dr. Hale by the whiteboard.
Press E or tap the button to talk.
